minutes.headline: Water commissioners approved the Hickory Hills pilot-study amendment, the Blue Leaf contract and the Tighe & Bond ARPA engineering proposal.
minutes.summary: The commissioners approved September 27 minutes and then took three PFAS-treatment votes: Tighe & Bond amendment number one, the Blue Leaf pilot study contract, and the Tighe & Bond proposal for the Keating well pilot, public education and master plan. They also heard about the lead service line survey, a new meter-reading system, PFAS test results, and the proposed water supply protection bylaw.

public_comment.topic: Asked for copies of the Tighe & Bond amendment, the Blue Leaf proposal and the Tighe & Bond Keating well study proposal; commissioners agreed to provide clean copies.
Asked about the proposed Water Supply Protection District map, the small circles on it, and why Zone 1 isn't in the bylaw; he plans to raise it with the Planning Board.

budget_items.what_was_said: The price rose for added work tied to the Conservation Commission notice of intent, hearings and appeal, offset in part by bench-scale testing shortening the pilot test.

budget_items.what_was_said: Contract for Blue Leaf to run the pilot test; the figure was read from the spreadsheet and stated differently in the captions.

budget_items.topic: Tighe & Bond proposal, Keating well pilot, public education and master plan (ARPA funded)
budget_items.what_was_said: Selectmen already approved ARPA funding for the work; the breakdown is pilot testing, public education and the master plan, with a deadline on use of the ARPA funds.
Test-hole excavation came in under budget, leaving grant funds for a postcard mailing to get residents to photograph their meters.
A downscaled version of the new system was described, with setup and annual per-customer fees; no vote was taken.
The engineer's request for additional compensation is still open; a commissioner thought the bill was extreme and no decision was made.

decisions.decision: No vote was needed on the Tighe & Bond ARPA proposal for the Keating well; commissioners were informed that it was moving ahead.
Agreed to ask Fuss & O'Neill whether the lead service line mailing can exclude residents who have already responded and newer-construction areas.
The Mass DOT/ SCADA-type item was held for a future meeting ('wait on that one'), and the new meter system was discussed as information only.
The commissioners left the engineering adjustment request unresolved.

what_happened.line: Commissioners passed Tighe & Bond amendment number one for the Hickory Hills wells pilot study, with two commissioners voting in favor.
Votes on the Blue Leaf pilot study contract and the Tighe & Bond Keating well proposal were not audible in the recording, so their outcomes are not confirmed.
The Tighe & Bond ARPA-funded Keating well pilot, public education and master plan proposal was reported as moving ahead, with selectmen having already approved the ARPA funding.
Commissioners agreed to ask Fuss & O'Neill whether the lead service line photo mailing can skip residents who already responded and newer-construction areas.
An engineer's request for additional compensation was left unresolved, and the new meter-reading system was discussed as information only.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills and Keating well pilot studies are the water district's PFAS-treatment path, and their contracts are what ratepayers' water bills will eventually carry.
The ARPA funds carry a deadline on use, and the lead service line survey asks residents to photograph their meters, so some households may be asked to act.
